paper_audit.verified_behavior: Four GraphLearn outputs are participant graphs, thresholded at cosine >0.9 and returned raw; GFR propagates full 320D concatenated features using normalize_adj(A+I), and i==1 overwrites i==0 combined_feat. medical_relation_rules.rule: Retain an undirected concept-level joint-deviation relation between frontoparietal/executive and cingulate-insular/salience candidate scores. Evaluate all four signed combinations without imposing a common ASD direction.

paper.citation: Coactivation pattern analysis reveals altered salience network dynamics in children with autism spectrum disorder (2021)
paper.finding: Dynamic coactivation configurations of the midcingulo-insular network with central-executive/lateral-frontoparietal systems appeared less frequently in the ASD group than TD.
paper.supports: A disease-relevant dynamic interaction hypothesis between salience-related and executive/frontoparietal systems.
paper.does_not_support: A universal direction for static FC edges, the exact Experiment 19 HO feature sets, or a direct correlation between the two domain deviation scores.

medical_relation_rules.measurable_with_current_features: Separate signed deviations can be computed for the frozen D2 and D4 FC feature sets and combined into four concept-level co-deviation channels. This measures joint occurrence, not network coactivation or a physical between-network edge.
medical_relation_rules.reason: The primary ASD study directly analyzes salience-midcingulo-insular and central-executive/lateral-frontoparietal coactivation; the current features support only a conservative concept-level test.

medical_relation_rules.rule: Retain an undirected concept-level joint-deviation relation between thalamocortical/sensorimotor and cingulate-insular/salience candidate scores. Evaluate all four signed combinations without imposing a common ASD direction.

papers.citation: Associations between thalamocortical functional connectivity and sensory over-responsivity in infants at high likelihood for ASD (2023)
papers.finding: Thalamic connectivity maps included sensory/motor, middle cingulate, insula and related regions; connectivity related to sensory over-responsivity in an infant high-likelihood design.
papers.supports: A cautious hypothesis that thalamocortical/sensory and cingulo-insular signals can jointly relate to sensory processing.
papers.does_not_support: A diagnosed-ASD-specific direction, current-sample patient labels, or a direct edge represented in the frozen feature set.

papers.citation: Salience Network Connectivity in Autism Is Related to Brain and Behavioral Markers of Sensory Over-Responsivity (2016)
papers.finding: Within ASD, sensory over-responsivity related to right anterior-insula connectivity with somatosensory/sensorimotor and temporal areas.
papers.supports: A sensory phenotype-specific salience-to-sensory interaction hypothesis.
papers.does_not_support: A universal ASD effect or a direct relation between all D3 and D4 candidate features.

medical_relation_rules.measurable_with_current_features: Separate signed deviations can be computed from D3 and D4 support sets and combined into four concept-level co-deviation channels. The two shared mapped feature slots (38 and 218) are not direct thalamus-insula connections; no cross-network FC edge is inferred.
medical_relation_rules.reason: Two primary studies connect thalamic/sensory and insular/salience evidence to sensory processing, while the protocol treats this as a hypothesis about co-deviation rather than direct network coupling.

method.location: after PLN InputLayer and before Encoder
method.td_reference: Ridge alpha=10 on age/site/sex PHENO one-hot, fit on outer-train TD only; train-TD residuals are fixed 5-fold OOF; train-ASD/test residuals use full outer-train TD fit; z uses OOF TD residual scale, clipped [-3,3].
method.interaction: signed u+/u- concept deviations above absolute z=1; 4 signed pair products; regress each product on 8 first-order scores using outer-train only, then center/scale on outer-train.
method.semantic_prior: two frozen undirected concept-level rules D2-D4 and D3-D4; no direction assumed; no physical between-network FC edge is inferred.
method.graph: same-fold K_sem from active signature; directed top-8 recipient-to-outer-train-source edges; row-normalized added branch. Existing raw GFR support is modulated by clipped 1+0.25*(K-center), and 0.25*K_sparse is added; original GFR symmetric normalize_adj(A+I) remains unchanged.
method.message: V_m=LayerNorm(Linear(X_m,36)); M_base_m=T_base_m@V_m; M_sem_m=T_sem_m@V_m; route weighted per-patient messages with a learned null plus four source logits; FULL uses M_sem-M_base.
method.residual: scale=RMS_train(H)/max(RMS_train(R),0.1*RMS_train(H)); detached scale; Delta=0.05*tanh(alpha)*R_hat, alpha[4]=0; each subject/token delta capped at 5% of H norm.
method.branch_parameters: four modality value projections, LayerNorms, one Linear router, alpha[4]; added PLN Adam group lr=.0038, weight_decay=0; same module shape in E1-E11.
method.original_graph_loss: unchanged GraphConstructLoss on the four original raw A_m matrices

worker_protocol: E0 runs first as one continuous 10-fold seed0 worker and snapshots full Python/NumPy/torch CPU/CUDA RNG before each construction. E1-E11 run independent continuous 10-fold workers, restoring the corresponding E0 fold-entry RNG before each construction; this is paired fold-entry control, not natural continuous cross-fold RNG.

decision.interpretation: The frozen method was evaluated as registered. The results do not satisfy all internal criteria for the claimed semantic and cross-source mechanism.
